sentences.text: Nafisa vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025

Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:2617
 1 M
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani

On The 7 th Of February, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 54480 of 2024
 Nafisa
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:

Shri Mayank Pathak - learned counsel for the applicant
 Shri Puran Kumar Kulshreshtha - learned Public Prosecu
 respondent/State.
 Order

1. This is second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of B.N.S.S./439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to Crime No.134/2024 registered at Police Station Mehgaon, District Bhind (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 366, 366A 376(d) and 506 of IPC and Section 3 /4 of POCSO Act.
2 As per story of prosecution, the allegation levelled against the applicant is that co-accused committed rape on exhortation of present applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that the first application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 6.9.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.32441 of 2024 by this Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:2617 2 MCRC-54480-2024 Thereafter two witnesses as prosecutrix (PW/1) and her mother (PW/2) have been examined before the trial Court.
They did not support the prosecution case and turn hostile.
The prosecutrix stated in her statement that she was aged about 19 years.

The mother of prosecutrix stated in her examination-in- chief that prosecutrix was of 16 to 17 years at the time of incident but she admits in her cross examination that prosecutrix was aged about 19 years at the time of incident and she denied that prosecutrix was of 14 year at the time of incident.
It is further submitted that though DNA report is positive in respect of co-accused but there is no evidence against the present applicant.
She has no criminal history.
She is in custody since 6.7.2024.

She is ready and willing to abide by all the terms and conditions which Nafisa vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143373173/
1 may be imposed by this Court.

sentences.text: Conclusion of the trial will take time.
On these grounds, learned counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac Only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.
In case, if she is found involved in the offence of same nature, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically without further reference to the Bench.

v) The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial;
vi) The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance, if possible, by the office of this Court.
Certified copy as per rules.
